text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. speaker: Doctor
text: That timing is highly suspicious for syncope triggered by a vagal maneuver. Did you experience any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath right before you passed out? Also, have you had any similar episodes in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vasovagal Syncope secondary to micturition (Tumultuous Voiding). The patient's rapid recovery without confusion, lack of incontinence, and specific timing immediately after urination strongly argue against a UTI and point toward a vagal response. While the previous physician's diagnosis of a UTI is unlikely given the absence of fever or dysuria, we should still rule out cardiac causes with an ECG before finalizing the plan.
